newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower for the third day in a row.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower for the third day in a row.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures posted losses for the third consecutive session on Tuesday, pressured by trade selling, floor sources said.
March delivery ended $6 a tonne lower, at $1,370, after ranging between $1,383 to $1,367. Second-month May fell $7, to close at $1,391, while the back months finished down $3 to $9.
Traders said a slightly disappointing Dutch 1996 fourth quarter 1996 cocoa grind, a key barometer of cocoa demand, may have weighed on the market.
The Dutch 1996 fourth quarter grind rose 3.90 percent to 97,273 tonnes compared with 93,619 tonnes in the same 1995 period, the Dutch Cocoa Association said on Tuesday.
The industry sources had forecast a fourth quarter rise of about five percent.
"The Dutch grind was not all that impressive. It was neutral at best," one trader said. "People were anticipating a slightly better number."
Traders await the German and U.K. 1996 fourth quarter cocoa grind data, slated for release later this week or early next week.
They expected the UK grind to fall by 10 percent on closure of one of Mars' plants and the German grind to fall by about two percent.
The U.S. fourth quarter grindings are due January 17.
On the charts, traders pegged March near-term support at $1,366-$1,362, then $1,350. To the upside, they said March would need to get by $1,390 and then $1,400 to spark substantial buying interest.
Turnover was moderate, at an estimated 8,739 lots. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
